name: Nine Five Two
description: Nine Five Two is a Canadian variation of Sergeant Major (8-5-3), a trick-taking game for three players with rotating targets. Each player has a specific trick quota: dealer needs 9, left opponent needs 5, right opponent needs 2. Players exchange cards based on overtricks/undertricks from previous hands. The game combines trick-taking skill with strategic card exchange.

history.origins: Nine Five Two is a Canadian variation of Sergeant Major (also known as 8-5-3), which originated in Britain's Royal Air Force. Sergeant Major itself was described as popular in the RAF, with related games (3-5-8) played in India and the Near East. The Canadian variant adjusts the targets to 9-5-2 and modifies the card exchange procedure.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Sergeant Major (8-5-3) popular in British RAF
Mid-20th Century: Game spreads to India and Near East as 3-5-8
Present: Played in Canada and by enthusiasts worldwide
history.cultural: Associated with military card game traditions, particularly RAF and Canadian forces. The quota system (different targets for different positions) reflects military hierarchy.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Sergeant Major by adjusting the target tricks (9-5-2 vs 8-5-3) and modifying when the dealer picks up the kitty (before discarding in 9-5-2). The scoring system also changed from per-hand settlement to cumulative points.

setup.players: 3 players. Targets: Dealer=9 tricks, Left opponent=5 tricks, Right opponent=2 tricks.
setup.dealing: 16 cards dealt to each player. Last 4 cards form the kitty. Dealer names trumps, picks up kitty, then discards 4 cards (this order is specific to 9-5-2).
setup.equipment: Standard deck, score pad for cumulative scoring.

rules.objective: Reach agreed target score (usually 10 or 20 points) by winning tricks relative to your quota.
rules.gameplay: 1. Dealer names trumps. 2. Player left of dealer leads to first trick. 3. Must follow suit if possible; may trump or discard if void. 4. Highest trump wins trick; otherwise highest of led suit wins. 5. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Dealer picks up kitty BEFORE discarding (unlike Sergeant Major)
Cumulative scoring: +1 per overtrick, -1 per undertrick
Card exchange based on over/under tricks

strategy.basic: Understand your target and play accordingly. If you need 9 tricks as dealer, you need a very strong hand. If you need only 2, you can play more defensively.
strategy.intermediate: Card exchange strategy: When giving cards to opponents who were down, give them cards that don't help their hand. When receiving cards, you must give back your highest of that suitâ€”manage your hand to minimize losses.
strategy.advanced: Track which cards have been exchanged to deduce opponents' holdings. Coordinate your play based on who needs to win tricks vs who is trying to avoid winning tricks.
tips: The dealer has the hardest target (9) but gets the kitty advantage
When you're 'down', try to give away low cards in suits where you have strength
The sum of all scores is always zeroâ€”if two players are positive, the third must be negative
